newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain hopes to sell Aldeasa 70 pct stake by Oct.
newsitem.headline: Spain hopes to sell Aldeasa 70 pct stake by Oct.

text.p: Spanish state holding company SEPPa plans to privatise its remaining 70 percent stake in duty-free shop operator Aldeasa by October, a spokesman said on Wednesday.

"We still have no fixed timetable but our aim is still to sell our stake at the end of September or the start of October," a spokesman for Sociedad Estatal de Participaciones Patrimoniales (SEPPa) told Reuters.

He added that SEPPa did not want the privatisation to coincide with the sale of partially-privatised utility Endesa, also set for autumn. A second state holding company plans to sell up to 35 percent of Endesa.
"At the moment, we are studying the time period (for the share offering) with global coordinator Warburg," he said.
The offer will be directed at domestic and international institutional investors, with a small tranche probably reserved for employees, the spokesman added.
Tabacalera paid an initial sum of 11.34 billion pesetas for a 20 percent stake in Aldeasa in June. The final price will be subject to the price set for the share offering.
Last week, SEPPa approved a capital increase in Aldeasa to which only Tabacalera could subscribe, lifting its stake from 20 to 30 percent.
Aldeasa forecasts a 22 percent rise in pretax profits to around 10 billion pesetas in 1997, with sales increasing to 60 billion pesetas.
